Designs using 1P mounting, which feature rows of single modules attached to torque tubes in a portrait orientation, tend to reduce steel racking requirements. In contrast, 2P designs, which feature rows of dual modules attached to torque tubes in a portrait orientation, reduce the number of piles per module string (Joe Shangraw 2024d). Figure 47 illustrates the two options. • Regardless of the module mounting configuration, the trend toward using significantly larger modules requires more structural steel. The growth of tracker use for elevated agrivoltaics systems also has potential to increase steel use (Chunduri and Schmela 2024). • Tracker systems are increasingly being installed on undulating or otherwise complex terrain, which—if the land is not graded extensively—requires using either longer piles or terrain-following trackers. Longer piles increase material use while terrain-following trackers require specialized structural components and tracking algorithms (Chunduri and Schmela 2024). • Global supply chain challenges have spurred a trend toward localizing tracker component production, which reduces transportation costs, delays in manufacturing and installation, and environmental impact (Chunduri and Schmela 2024). 69 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
